He played [[college football]] for the [[Butte College|Butte Roadrunners]] and the [[Sonoma State Cossacks football|Sonoma State Cossacks]], and was selected by the Cowboys in the second round of the [[1994 NFL draft]]. A player capable of using his speed against defenders, Allen was regarded as one of the strongest players to ever play in the NFL,{{cite web|url=http://www.criticalbench.com/Larry-Allen-Bench-Press.htm|title = Larry Allen's Bench Press| date=December 8, 2023 }}{{Cite news |last=Aron |first=Jaime |date=July 29, 2001 |title=700-pound bench press makes Cowboys OL Allen noteworthy powerlifter, too |work=Abilene Reporter-News |url=http://www.texnews.com/1998/2001/cowboys/make0729.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110614100744/http://www.texnews.com/1998/2001/cowboys/make0729.html |archive-date=June 14, 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://www.sonoma.edu/newscenter/2013/02/post-179.html|title=Larry Allen's long road from SSU to the NFL Hall of Fame.|website=www.sonoma.edu|first=Bob|last=Padecky|date=February 2, 2013|access-date=April 27, 2016}}{{Citation |last=NFL World |title=DeMarcus Ware shares who is the greatest player he ever faced |date=September 16, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PxDG5iy56jc |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010192721/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PxDG5iy56jc |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 10, 2023 |access-date=October 4, 2017}} and has been ranked as the best offensive lineman of all-time by [[Fox Sports]].{{cite web | title=Who are the 10 best offensive lineman of all-time? | publisher=FOX Sports | date=2024-12-16 | url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/who-10-greatest-nfl-offensive-linemen-all-time | access-date=2026-05-14}} Spending his first 12 seasons with the Cowboys, Allen earned ten [[Pro Bowl]] selections and six first-team [[All-Pro]] honors. He was also part of the team that won a [[Super Bowl]] title in [[Super Bowl XXX]] over the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. Allen played his final two seasons with the [[San Francisco 49ers]], where he received his 11th Pro Bowl selection. He was inducted to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2013.{{Cite news |last=Corbett |first=Jim |date=February 2, 2013 |title=Parcells, Carter finally make Pro Football Hall of Fame |work=USA Today |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2013/02/02/nfl-hall-of-fame-announcement/1886453/ |access-date=February 2, 2013}}

'''Larry Eugene Centers''' (born June 1, 1968) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 14 seasons, mostly the [[Arizona Cardinals|Phoenix / Arizona Cardinals]] (1990–1998). Centers then played for the [[Washington Commanders|Washington Redskins]] (1999–2000), the [[Buffalo Bills]] (2001–2002), and finally was a member of the [[New England Patriots]], with whom he won a Super Bowl.

Centers played [[college football]] for the [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks football|Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks]]. One of the most prolific pass catching [[running back]]s in NFL history, he topped 100 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] in 1995 and had 99 receptions in 1996. He owns the NFL record for most passes caught by a running back during a career.<ref name="mainsourceBuffalo">{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-22381110.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140611091031/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-22381110.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 11, 2014|title=Catch Him if you Can; For Ageless Larry Centers, It's Better to Be On The Receiving End|last=Gleason|first=Bucky|date=November 25, 2001|work=The Buffalo News|access-date=March 6, 2014}}</ref> He was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] in 1995, 1996, and 2001.

'''Larry Lavern Ball''' (born September 27, 1949) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Louisville Cardinals football|Louisville Cardinals]].

Ball was selected in the [[1972 NFL draft]] by the [[Miami Dolphins]]. He also played for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and the [[Detroit Lions]]. During his [[National Football League]] (NFL) career, he participated in 79 games. Ball is the only player in NFL history to play an entire season for both an undefeated team, the [[1972 Miami Dolphins season|1972 Miami Dolphins]] (where he won [[Super Bowl VII]]), and a winless team, the [[1976 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|1976 Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. ([[Maulty Moore]] also played for the 1972 Dolphins and 1976 Buccaneers, but while he was with the Dolphins for the entire 1972 season, he was signed by the '76 Bucs late in the season, playing in only five games, starting only in the final game. A third player who also played for the '72 Dolphins, [[Doug Swift]], was taken by the Buccaneers in the expansion draft, but retired from football to enter medical school and never reported to the team.)<ref>{{cite news |last=Martz |first=Ron |title=Bear sizes up the Bucs |newspaper=St. Petersburg Times |date=17 July 1976 }}</ref>

After football, Ball worked as a guidance counselor, department head, and coach for Miami-Dade County Public Schools in [[Miami, Florida]]. He retired in 2011 after more than 30 years of service. He is active in the South Florida community, participating in numerous charity events along with his fellow '72 Undefeated Team teammates.

'''Langston Moore''' (born July 19, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]] and was selected 174th overall by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the sixth round of the [[2003 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Arizona Cardinals]], [[Detroit Lions]] and [[Florida Tuskers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2003 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2003/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Moore attended James Island [[Charter High School of the Arts|Charter High School]] in [[Charleston, South Carolina]], where he lettered in football and was a standout in Region AAAA play. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of South Carolina]]. Moore graduated from University of South Carolina in 2003.

He joined the Gamecock IMG Sports Network in 2012 as the sideline reporter for football broadcasts.

His father was the Ft. Wayne WOWO Radio and Charleston radio personality, Ken Moore.
